'''Michele Rajna''' (September 28, 1854 – September 29, 1920) was an Italian [[Mathematics|mathematician]] and [[astronomer]]. He led astronomy at the [[University of Bologna]] for nearly two decades, publishing studies of [[Eclipse|eclipses]], [[Earth's magnetic field]], and [[geodetic astronomy]]. He was the director of the [[Observatory of Bologna]] from 1903 until his death.

==Early life and education==

Rajna was born in [[Sondrio]], a city in the [[Kingdom of Lombardy–Venetia]] in the [[Austrian Empire]], in 1854.<ref name=":3">{{cite web |title=Michele Rajna |url=https://archiviostoricoastronomia.unibo.it/cenni/direttori/michele_rajna |website=University of Bologna |publisher=Historical Archives of the Department of Astronomy |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref> He was the second-born son of Eugenio Paolo Rajna and Costanza Simonetta. His older brother [[Pio Rajna]], born 1847, was an Italian [[Philology|philologist]] and [[Literary criticism|literary critic]] who later served in the [[Senate of the Kingdom of Italy]]. 

He attended [[Ghislieri College]] in [[Pavia]], where he studied under astronomer [[Giovanni Schiaparelli]] at the [[Brera Astronomical Observatory]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":1">{{cite book |last1=Mazliak |first1=Laurent |last2=Tazzioli |first2=Rossana |title=Mathematicians at war: Volterra and his French colleagues in World War I |date=8 October 2009 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-90-481-2740-5 |page=149 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Mathematicians_at_war/JqlodyLh7O4C?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA149&printsec=frontcover |access-date=31 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Rajna attended the [[University of Pavia]], graduating with a [[doctor of science|doctorate]] in mathematics in 1878.<ref name=":0">{{cite book |title=Terrestrial Magnetism and Atmospheric Electricity |date=1904 |publisher=University of Michigan |page=144 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Terrestrial_Magnetism_and_Atmospheric_El/SB3OAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA144&printsec=frontcover |access-date=30 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Society |first1=Manchester Literary and Philosophical |title=Memoirs and Proceedings of the Manchester Literary & Philosophical Society |date=1891 |publisher=The Society |page=314 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Memoirs_and_Proceedings_of_the_Mancheste/hOsAAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA314-IA6&printsec=frontcover |access-date=30 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Upon graduating from the University of Pavia, Rajna joined the Brera Astronomical Observatory in 1878.<ref>{{cite book |title=The American Meteorological Journal |date=1885 |publisher=W.H. Burr |page=546 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_American_Meteorological_Journal/Lqg9AQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA546&printsec=frontcover |access-date=31 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> In 1882, he was appointed Third Astronomer at the observatory and recognized for his mathematical work on [[Cartesian coordinate system|Cartesian coordinate]] calculation by an invitation to join the Italian Geodetic Commission.<ref name=":3" /> He became a lecturer in astronomy and geodesy at the [[Polytechnic University of Milan]] in 1890.<ref name=":3" /> Wishing to remain in [[Milan]], in 1897 he rejected an offer to chair the astronomy department at the [[University of Palermo]]. 

Rajna became chair of astronomy at the [[University of Bologna]] in 1903.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> He wrote a letter supporting the [[Vatican Observatory]] in 1907.<ref>{{cite book |last1=J |first1=Gabriele Gionti, S. |last2=S.J |first2=Jean-Baptiste Kikwaya Eluo |title=The Vatican Observatory, Castel Gandolfo: 80th Anniversary Celebration |date=4 January 2018 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-67205-2 |page=225 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Vatican_Observatory_Castel_Gandolfo/p41FDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA225&printsec=frontcover |access-date=31 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He directed the [[Observatory of Bologna]] until his death, attempting unsuccessfully to have it transferred to Villa Aldini, a more suitable position on a nearby hill.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Malaspina |first1=Marco |last2=Galleti |first2=Silvia |title=Why an Astronomical Station in Loiano? |url=https://www.oas.inaf.it/en/about-us/loiano-telescopes/the-60-cm-telescope/why-an-astronomical-station-in-loiano/ |website=INAF OAS Bologna |publisher=Institute Nazionale di Astronomia |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> A branch was later built in [[Loiano]] in 1933 by his successor, [[Guido Horn d'Arturo]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Museo della Specola, Bologna - Storia cap. 17 |url=https://museospecola.difa.unibo.it/english/sto2_17.html |website=museospecola.difa.unibo.it |publisher=University of Bologna |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref>

Rajna's work focused primarily on [[geodetic astronomy]] and the influence of [[Solar phenomena|solar activity]] on [[Earth's magnetic field]].<ref>{{cite web |title=La Specola, Bologna Observatory, Italy |url=https://web.astronomicalheritage.net/show-entity?identity=213&idsubentity=1 |website=UNESCO |publisher=UNESCO Portal to the Heritage of Astronomy - Show entity |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=Ernest W. |title=Review: Michele Rajna, L'Ora Esatta Dappertutto, etc. |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |date=January 1900 |volume=5 |issue=5 |url=https://www.projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society/volume-5/issue-5/Review-Michele-Rajna-LOra-Esatta-Dappertutto-etc/bams/1183415719.full |access-date=30 March 2026 |language=en |issn=0002-9904}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=The Geographical Journal |date=1900 |publisher=Royal Geographical Society. |page=88 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Geographical_Journal/LRUSAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA88&printsec=frontcover |access-date=31 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He found a method to graphically predict [[solar eclipses]] in 1891.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rajna |first1=Michele |title=On Solar Eclipses |date=1891 |publisher=University of Michigan |page=9 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Pamphlets_Astronomy/IzDOAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=RA5-PA1&printsec=frontcover |access-date=31 March 2026 |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Michele |first1=Rajna |title=Sulle eclissi solari del 6 giugno 1891 e del 16 aprile 1893 / nota del s.c. dott. Michele Rajna |journal=opac.museogalileo.it |date=1891 |volume=2 |issue=24 |page=16 |url=https://opac.museogalileo.it/imss/resource?uri=352269&v=l&dcnr=0 |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Publications |journal=Astronomical Society of the Pacific |date=November 18, 1891 |volume=3 |page=329 |doi=10.1086/120346/pdf |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/120346/pdf |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> He published a volume of [[logarithm]] tables to five decimals with Otto Müller through [[Hoepli Editore]] in 1883 which became one of the most commonly used computational aids in Italy for decades.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Recent Mathematical Tables |journal=Mathematical Tables and Other Aids to Computation |date=1948 |volume=3 |issue=21 |pages=19–40 |doi=10.2307/2002658 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2002658 |access-date=30 March 2026 |issn=0891-6837}}</ref> It was republished in 1886 and again in 1891.<ref>{{cite web |title=Recent Mathematical Tables |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/1948-03-021/S0025-5718-48-99561-1/S0025-5718-48-99561-1.pdf |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=30 March 2026}}</ref> Rajna also published a volume calculating the true geographical [[local time]] of any place in Italy.<ref>{{cite book |title=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |date=1899 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |pages=260-261 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Bulletin_of_the_American_Mathematical_So/v8ZNAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA260&printsec=frontcover |access-date=30 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He was a member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei|Italian National Academy]].<ref name=":2">{{cite book |last1=Lockyer |first1=Sir Norman |title=Nature |date=1921 |publisher=Macmillan Journals Limited |page=511 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Nature/AnC1zRpCkAwC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=michele+rajna&pg=PA511&printsec=frontcover |access-date=31 March 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

After frequent periods of [[Depression (mood)|depression]] and illness,<ref name=":3" /> Rajna died on September 20, 1920, in [[Teglio]], Italy.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />
